connections.name: Wh- Question Formation and Auxiliary Inversion
connections.teacher_explanation: In both Unit 1 and Unit 6, students form information questions by placing a question word (What, When, Where, Who, How many) followed by an inverted auxiliary or linking verb (is, are, do, does) before the subject. Recognizing this structural inversion pattern helps students formulate accurate questions across different communicative contexts.

connections.name: Present Simple Third-Person Singular Subject-Verb Agreement (-s / -es)
connections.teacher_explanation: In Unit 6, students learn the rule of adding -s/-es to present simple verbs with third-person singular subjects (he/she/it) when describing personal schedules and mechanisms. In Unit 8, this exact inflectional rule applies when describing animal habitats (e.g., 'A fox lives...' vs. 'Whales live...'). Linking these structures reinforces that third-person singular verb marking is a general grammatical constraint across both daily actions and factual science descriptions.

connections.name: Pronoun-Referent Agreement Across Singular and Plural Subjects
connections.teacher_explanation: Unit 1 requires students to differentiate singular referents (he/she) from plural groups (they) when asking and answering about continuous actions. Unit 8 similarly requires selecting singular 'it' versus plural 'they' when answering ability questions about animals. Teachers can highlight how English systematically tracks number across question frames and short answers using pronoun substitution.

connections.name: Pronoun Contractions with Present Tense Copular / Helping Verbs
connections.teacher_explanation: Unit 1 explicitly practices personal pronoun contractions with 'be' (he's, she's, they're) in continuous statements. Unit 6 focuses on the dummy/impersonal pronoun contraction 'It's' (it is) for telling time and describing clock instruments. Both skills involve recognizing that the apostrophe replaces the missing vowel in spoken and written contracted forms.

connections.name: Phonemic Blending of Multi-Letter Digraphs to Read Words
connections.teacher_explanation: Units 1, 6, and 8 provide structured phonics practice requiring learners to blend phonemes containing multi-letter digraphs and trigraphs (unvoiced/voiced 'th' in Unit 1, 'ch', 'tch', and 'sh' in Unit 6, and 'ou' and 'ow' in Unit 8). The underlying mechanical skill—holding onset and rime digraph sounds in working memory and synthesizing them into whole words—is a shared phonological skill across all three units.

connections.name: Interactive Pairwork Command: 'ask and answer'
connections.teacher_explanation: The instructional routine 'ask and answer' is used identically across Units 1, 6, and 8 to initiate paired oral interaction where one learner prompts with the unit's target question frame and the partner formulates the corresponding target response. Recognizing this prompt allows students to execute collaborative speaking tasks without requiring explicit teacher re-direction.

connections.name: Phonics Decoding Task Command: 'blend the sounds'
connections.teacher_explanation: The instructional command 'blend the sounds' appears consistently on page 17 of Unit 1, page 103 of Unit 6, and page 141 of Unit 8. It cues learners to perform the specific phonics routine of synthesizing isolated sounds into fluent spoken words. Internalizing this command enables students to engage in independent decoding during phonics lessons.

connections.name: Chronological and Numerical Ordering Task Command: 'number in order' / 'number'
connections.teacher_explanation: In Units 1, 6, and 8, learners encounter the task directive to number pictures or items in sequence based on an audio narrative. Comprehension of this instruction signals to students that the task requires sequencing chronological events rather than matching or circling items.

evidence_gaps.description: Verifying the chronological sequence required by 'number in order' and 'number' activities across Unit 1 (Activity 28), Unit 6 (Activity 29), and Unit 8 (Activity 29) depends on audio tracks that were identified as gaps in the individual unit source analyses.
